newsitem.title: UK: Poster ad "unfairly denigrated" BT, watchdog says.
newsitem.headline: Poster ad "unfairly denigrated" BT, watchdog says.

text.p: A British cable television and phone service provider unfairly denigrated its competitor, British Telecommunications Plc, by using the headline "British Telecon" in a poster advertisement, a watchdog group said on Saturday.

The Advertising Standards Authority (ASA) said in its monthly report that it had upheld complaints made by BT and one member of the public. The ASA said the adverts "unfairly denigrated BT", and it asked that the advertising campaign be dropped.

Bell Cablemedia Plc, in a poster advertising campaign promoting its phone service, used the headlines "British Telecon," "The Great Phone Robbery, BT's profits soar to nearly two billion pounds" and "Last Year BT's earnings were 3,000,000,000 pounds."
The ads were created by Rapier, Stead & Bowden.
British Telecommunications, Britain's biggest phone operator, is often referred to as British Telecom.
The ASA also upheld a complaint over a press advert for safety glasses that showed a photo of Prince Charles wearing a pair of the glasses.
The advertiser, Uvex (UK) Ltd, said it believed it had the right to use the photo of Prince Charles, because it had appeared in a national newspaper.
The ASA, however, said that although the ad did not imply an endorsement by Prince Charles, permission was still required from the Britain's royal family for the use of photographs in adverts.

The ASA said it upheld complaints over three advertisements for a computer game called Re-Loaded. The ads appeared in PC Gamer magazine and used violent imagery, including a robot holding a severed head and a female character holding a knife and a gun, and sitting astride a giant skull.
The three ads carried the strapline "You got even. Now get Re-Loaded."
